column7: Bounds what an untrusted provider can put in the log and in the error a login ends with: only a listed RFC 6749 error code passes, any other text reads as other
Refuses an authorization code from another issuer before redeeming it (RFC 9207 issuer check, validate_issuer at its call here), on every login path: CLI, startup and the web UI
Says whether a sign-in was confirmed since this client last adopted from storage, so its cached token may be an older account; a mistake would keep sending the old credential

Takes the confirmed token from storage for a client holding an older one, sampling the install count before the read and recording it only after; a mistake would keep the old credential or lose a newer confirm
Says whether the latest confirmed sign-in was saved under another issuer than the one this client discovered, so no credential of either issuer is used across the boundary
Adopts a confirmed sign-in only if re-discovery names the install's issuer; otherwise fails closed with the sign-in wait, drops the in-memory token and raises the provider-changed reason
Stops discovery on a destination-policy (SSRF) refusal and on a refused advertised endpoint instead of walking past it; the check moved here from initialize
Records the explicit sign-in-required reason after a failed-closed re-discovery; a mistake would hide it
Ends the provider-changed reason only when an install under the client's own issuer is adopted; a mistake would clear it early
Refuses a token obtained across an await once a sign-in under another issuer was confirmed meanwhile; a mistake would hand the previous issuer's credential to a call after the switch.
Refuses a cached, adopted or refreshed token to detached work a restart or stop revoked, then rechecks the issuer; a mistake would hand a token to cancelled work.
Ends a detached stage on a restart or stop and at the authorization window or deadline, read through classify; a mistake would let a stage outlive its cancel or its bound.
